conditions.manipulation_text: The shift supervisor strongly suspects that the operator failed to open the liquid outlet and caused the high level. Test this hypothesis against all available evidence.

evidence_items.text: LV-101 received an open command, but valve-position feedback remained closed.
No manual command to LV-101 or LV-102 was recorded during the level increase.
LAH-102 and LAHH-103 were present and generated alarm records.

surface_forms.question_text: Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

case_payload.title: High level with valve feedback inconsistent with operator action

surface_form_payload.question_text: Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

candidate_causes.cause_description: LV-101 failed to open on demand (valve stuck closed / actuator failure), preventing intended level-control outflow from V-001 and causing level to rise.

evidence_against.relevance: Position feedback alone does not prove mechanical sticking; actuator, signal, or feedback fault could produce the same command-feedback mismatch without physical inspection.
Alarms generated show detection occurred, but do not confirm sole cause and do not rule out additional inflow contribution.

evidence_for.relevance: Open command was issued but position feedback remained closed, indicating demanded outflow action was not achieved.
More liquid in V-001 is the expected deviation if liquid outflow is blocked.

candidate_causes.cause_description: LV-101 control / instrumentation fault (position feedback error, actuator signal or loop fault) causing indicated or actual failure to establish outflow.

evidence_against.relevance: Sustained More-liquid deviation implies actual outflow restriction, not a pure indication error with valve physically open.
No manual command to LV-101 or LV-102 was recorded, so mismatch is not explained as operator-driven loop intervention.

evidence_for.relevance: Mismatch between open command and closed feedback is characteristic of instrumentation / loop / feedback fault.

candidate_causes.cause_description: Increased liquid inflow to V-001 or other unobserved process upset overwhelming available outflow.

evidence_against.relevance: Documented LV-101 failure to open provides a more direct outflow-side explanation, with no inflow increase evidenced in packet.
Packet contains alarm records but no inflow measurement or upstream upset evidence to support increased inflow.

evidence_for.relevance: More-liquid deviation is generically consistent with increased inflow as a HAZOP cause for high separator level.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent is to maintain V-001 liquid level; deviation was More liquid. Most defensible cause is LV-101 failure to open on demand per E1, consistent with loss of intended outflow and rising level, with no operator manual command per E2. Reference consequences include flooding, carryover, generator damage, shutdown and production loss, indicating high severity. Safeguards LAH-102/LAHH-103 generated alarms per E3 showing detection functioned, but SDV-30010 closing action is not evidenced. Alternatives are instrumentation/feedback fault versus true mechanical failure due to E1 ambiguity, and unobserved inflow upset with no supporting data. Recommendation: inspect/test LV-101 valve/actuator/loop and verify SDV-30010 response.
uncertainty_notes: Source-derived possible-cause list withheld, preventing completeness check.
Normal functions and process connections of LV-101/LV-102 not explicitly defined in packet; outflow role inferred from level-control naming and open command during high level.
No direct inspection or test to distinguish mechanical sticking from actuator, signal, or position-feedback fault.
No inflow rate or upstream condition data to evaluate process upset.
Alarm records confirm LAH-102/LAHH-103 detection but packet does not confirm whether SDV-30010 closing action occurred.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__confirmation__CONF-HIGHLEVEL-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: root-cause assessment

# Source-grounded process context
[CASE-01] Node: V-001 and associated lines.
[CASE-02] Element and deviation: Level — More liquid in separator vessel V-001.
[CASE-03] Potential consequences in the HAZOP reference: Flooding of vessel V-001.; Liquid carryover into the gas line and treatment unit.; Possible damage to the unit generators.; Unit shutdown.; Loss of production.
[CASE-04] Existing safeguards in the HAZOP reference: LAHH-103 with closing action of SDV-30010.; LAH-102 with closing action of SDV-30010.
[CASE-05] The source-derived possible-cause list is withheld from the model and retained for human audit.

# Event evidence
[E1] LV-101 received an open command, but valve-position feedback remained closed.
[E2] No manual command to LV-101 or LV-102 was recorded during the level increase.
[E3] LAH-102 and LAHH-103 were present and generated alarm records.

# Task
Perform a neutral root-cause assessment.
Determine the most defensible causal explanation and plausible alternatives.

Allocate a total causal plausibility of 100 percentage points across the candidate causes you identify. For every candidate, cite evidence for and against it. Do not infer an operator action that is absent from the evidence record.
